sentences.text:
Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya vs Virendra Kumar Jain on 6
July, 2017
 Crr-2642-2015
 (Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya Vs Virendra Kumar Jain)
06-07-2017
 Shri Ramesh Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners.
 Shri Aman Chouraisa, learned counsel for respondent No.1.
Ms. Sharda Dueby, learned Panel Lawyer for respondent No.2/State.

This revision under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Cr.P.C. has been directed against order
dated 17/03/2015 passed by Second Asj, Sagar in Criminal Revision No.81/2015, setting aside
order dated 19/02/2015 passed by learned Jmfc, Sagar in criminal Case No.2192/2014.
Brief facts just necessary for disposal of this petition are that the respondent No.1 is the shopkeeper.

The Food Inspector has bought the pouch of Pan Masala from the shop of respondent No.1 when the
sample was sent for analysis to the Food Testing Laboratory, Bhopal it was found to be unsafe for
human consumption as 3.408% Magnesium Carbonate (Mgco3) was found in it.

He filed a
criminal complaint before the learned Jmfc for offence under Section 26(2) (1)/59 of Food Safety
and Standards Act, 2006.

The respondent No.1 then filed an application under Section 319 of
Cr.P.C. stating that he is not the manufacturer of the Food Article Pan Parag.

He claimed to be only
the shopkeeper and alleging that the manufacturer and packing was done by the present petitioners.

He requested the Court to implead the company Pan Parag and its manufacturer, as accused in the
case.

The learned Jmfc after affording opportunity to the prosecution passed the order stating that
evidence has not been recorded in the case in hand.

The impleading of any additional person as a
co-accused
can only arise after recording evidence

, therefore, application under Section 319 of
Cr.P.C. is not maintainable.

The accused/respondent No.1 filed criminal revision No.91/2015, learned Second Asj, Sagar vide
order dated 27/08/2015 has held that the manufacturer of Pan Parag Pan Masala is a company and
by virtue of Section 66 of the Food Standard and Safety Act, 2006 and is Managing Director may be
prosecuted.

The Revisional Court further held that jurisdiction to take cognizance of offence against
person not named as accused whose complicity in case could be evidence from the material on
record, even without recording evidence.

He referred the case of Dharam Pal & others Vs. State of
Haryana & another reported as (2014) 3 Scc 306.

He concluded that the order of learned Jmfc
suffers from illegality and incorrectness and setting aside the same directed the trial Court to array
the Managing Director of Pan Parag India Ltd. and proceed with the matter according to law.

The authorized representative of the company Pan Parag India Ltd. and the Managing Director of
Pan Parag Ltd. have moved this revision in this background, it is claimed that the learned Revisional
Court erred in passing the order impugned.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The decision rendered by Honble Supreme Court in
Dharam Pal (supra) has been misconstrued.

It is also claimed that the learned Jmfc summoned the
petitioners who were not included in the charge-sheet.

No evidence has been recorded under Section
200 & 202 of Cr.P.C., therefore, it is not a fit case to issue summons.

It is further claimed that no
prima facie case is made out against the petitioner.

Learned counsel for the petitioner argued that in the case of Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab
reported as Air 2014 Sc 1400, it has been made clear that the power under Section 319 of Cr.P.C.
can only be exercised on the basis of fresh evidence brought before the Court.

entities.text:
Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab
reported as Air 2014 Sc 1400
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further claimed that the learned Revisional Court passed the order impugned erroneously.

The
application under Section 319 of Cr.P.C. during the course of enquiry remains limited to the extend
that adding a person as an accused whose name has been mentioned in column No.2 of the
charge-sheet or any other person who might be accomplished.

Per contra, learned Panel Lawyer for respondent/State vehemently opposed the contentions and
submit that the learned Revisional Court has analyzed the legal aspects and allowed the revision
which is not called for any interference.
Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.1 also submits that the order of the Revisional Court
is based on the verdict of the 5 members Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in Dharam Pal is

case (supra) in which it has been held that even without recording evidence, upon committal under
Section 209 of Cr.P.C., the Session Judge may summon those persons shown in Column No.2 of
Police report
to stand trial along with those already named therein.

For all offences, the Court of
Magistrate is competent to arraign person as an accused from and during stage of cognizance itself
under Section 190 of Cr.P.C.
Following the law laid down in Dharam Pal's case (supra), the learned Revisional Court has passed
the order.
There fore, no interference is called for.
This petition is dismissed.

SUSHIL KUMAR PALO) JUDGE RS Anand Vikram Singh Bhadoriya vs Virendra Kumar Jain on 6 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35903248/
